ocr.notes: Mostly readable; scattered garbled words and phrases (e.g. 'couple of thousand dollars', 'Indian Territory', 'caught napping')

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Globe-Democrat reported that Tom Allen denied reports of a fight with Jem Mace, saying he would not fight in the East but would back himself if Mace fought in the Indian Territory.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Daily Globe-Democrat, Sunday Morning, December 26, 187[5] (last digit faint; Sunday fits 1875)

facts.fact: Allen told a Globe-Democrat reporter he had done nothing to bring out a challenge from Jem Mace and had not heard from him in any official manner
Allen said he would not fight Mace in the East but was willing to back himself for a couple of thousand dollars if Mace would fight in the Indian Territory or another Western or Southwestern region
Mace had published a card announcing he was coming to America to fight Allen for the championship of the world
The previous summer Rooke and the New York gang failed to appear for a fight with Allen and the stakeholder was enjoined from handing over the stakes
Allen confirmed he was to appear on stage in a sensational play written for him, playing a 'rough diamond' who rescues the heroine, under the supervision of a leading actress

notes: Contradicts 527/528 (match with Mace made in Chicago Nov. 1875); this article says no definite action taken beyond Mace's card. No verbatim Allen quotes; his remarks are paraphrased.
